A 18-year-old male is evaluated in the emergency department following a high-speed motor vehicle
accident where he was an unrestrained driver. He was extricated from the vehicle and presents with

severe upper back pain and lower extremity paralysis. His vital signs show: pulse 50/min, respirations
13/min, blood pressure 80/51 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. The patient is alert and
oriented, with his cervical spine immobilized. Physical examination reveals: - Flaccid paralysis and
absent reflexes in lower extremities - Loss of sensation below nipple level, including perianal region -
No anal tone on rectal exam - No anal sphincter response to glans penis squeeze - Normal
cardiopulmonary findings - Soft abdomen - FAST scan negative CT imaging shows an isolated burst
fracture of T3 vertebra without facet involvement. After initiating intravenous fluid therapy, what is the
most appropriate next management step? Answer Choices: (A) Emergency decompressive
laminectomy (B) Administration of mannitol (C) Administration of vasopressors (D) Application of
pneumatic compression devices (E) Placement of Foley catheter (F) Intubation and mechanical
ventilation (G) Immediate MRI of the thoracic spine (H) Surgical stabilization of the spine (I)
Administration of methylprednisolone (J) Intravenous dexamethasone therapy
 A. Administration of mannitol
B. Immediate MRI of the thoracic spine
C. Intravenous dexamethasone therapy
D. Placement of Foley catheter
E. Surgical stabilization of the spine
F. Emergency decompressive laminectomy
G. Intubation and mechanical ventilation
H. Application of pneumatic compression devices
I. Administration of methylprednisolone
J. Administration of vasopressors
